---
title: "Acquire SWISSIMAGE orthophotos"
description: "Discover, download and mosaic intersecting orthophoto tiles."
---

<div class="toolbox-kind">Recipe · verified 2026-10-04</div>

## Goal

Select SWISSIMAGE tiles by polygon or bbox, choose an explicit resolution, download the Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs, and create a mosaic with optional clipping.

The verified collection is:

```text
ch.swisstopo.swissimage-dop10
```

It contains 1 km tiles in LV95 (`EPSG:2056`) with 0.1 m and 2 m COG assets. The native product is 10 cm in the plain and main alpine valleys and 25 cm over the Alps; the asset metadata still labels the high-resolution option with `gsd: 0.1`.

## Discover tiles

Reuse `search_stac()` from the [generic geo.admin STAC recipe](geoadmin-stac.qmd). `intersects` must be a WGS84 GeoJSON geometry.

```{python}
#| eval: false
COLLECTION = "ch.swisstopo.swissimage-dop10"


def tile_id(item):
    return item["id"].rsplit("_", 1)[-1]


def latest_per_tile(items):
    ordered = sorted(
        items,
        key=lambda item: item["properties"]["datetime"],
        reverse=True,
    )
    selected = {}
    for item in ordered:
        selected.setdefault(tile_id(item), item)
    return list(selected.values())


items = search_stac(
    collection=COLLECTION,
    intersects=intersects,
    sortby="-properties.datetime",
)
items = latest_per_tile(items)

[(item["id"], item["properties"]["datetime"]) for item in items]
```

The acquisition year can vary between adjacent tiles because SWISSIMAGE is updated on a cycle. Inspect the selected dates before treating the mosaic as one simultaneous image. For a historical comparison, pass an explicit `datetime` interval and do not collapse to the latest item.

## Choose the resolution explicitly

Filter on asset `gsd`, not filename text or list position.

```{python}
#| eval: false
def select_swissimage_assets(items, gsd):
    selected = []

    for item in items:
        matches = [
            (asset_key, asset)
            for asset_key, asset in item["assets"].items()
            if asset.get("gsd") == gsd
            and asset.get("type", "").startswith("image/tiff")
        ]
        if len(matches) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected one {gsd} m COG for {item['id']}, found {len(matches)}"
            )

        asset_key, asset = matches[0]
        selected.append(
            {
                "item_id": item["id"],
                "tile_id": tile_id(item),
                "datetime": item["properties"]["datetime"],
                "asset_key": asset_key,
                "gsd": asset["gsd"],
                "epsg": asset.get("proj:epsg"),
                "checksum": asset.get("file:checksum"),
                "href": asset["href"],
            }
        )

    if any(asset["epsg"] != 2056 for asset in selected):
        raise ValueError("Unexpected CRS")
    return selected


# Use 2 m for lightweight exploration; request 0.1 only when needed.
assets = select_swissimage_assets(items, gsd=2.0)
assets
```

A verified example 1 km tile was approximately 150 KB at 2 m and 63 MB at 0.1 m. Estimate the tile count and storage before selecting the high-resolution assets.

## Save the manifest and download

```{python}
#| eval: false
import json
from pathlib import Path

import requests

raw_dir = Path("input/raw/swissimage")
raw_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

(raw_dir / "selected_assets.json").write_text(
    json.dumps(assets, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False),
    encoding="utf-8",
)


def download_asset(url, destination):
    destination = Path(destination)
    if destination.exists():
        raise FileExistsError(destination)

    with requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=120) as response:
        response.raise_for_status()
        with destination.open("wb") as file:
            for chunk in response.iter_content(chunk_size=1024 * 1024):
                if chunk:
                    file.write(chunk)


for asset in assets:
    download_asset(asset["href"], raw_dir / asset["asset_key"])
```

The assets are COGs, so GDAL can also read selected byte ranges remotely through `/vsicurl/`. Downloading first is usually clearer and more reproducible for a project input directory.

## Inspect and mosaic

Check a tile before building the mosaic:

```bash
gdalinfo input/raw/swissimage/example_2_2056.tif
```

Create a virtual mosaic, then materialize it as one COG only when a single file is useful:

```bash
gdalbuildvrt output/swissimage.vrt input/raw/swissimage/*.tif

gdal_translate output/swissimage.vrt output/swissimage.tif \
  -of COG -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co QUALITY=90 \
  -co BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER
```

Keep the VRT when downstream software can use it: materializing a 10 cm mosaic can create a very large duplicate.

## Optional crop or mask

The STAC polygon search selects intersecting 1 km tiles; it does not clip them. Keeping complete tiles is often desirable. When the exact study-area shape is needed:

```bash
gdalwarp output/swissimage.vrt output/swissimage_clipped.tif \
  -cutline input/processed/study_area.gpkg \
  -crop_to_cutline -dstalpha \
  -of COG -co COMPRESS=JPEG -co QUALITY=90 \
  -co BIGTIFF=IF_SAFER
```

Do not reproject unless the next operation requires another CRS. If reprojection is necessary, set the intended resolution and alignment explicitly rather than accepting accidental defaults.

## What was tested

- STAC v1 collection metadata and spatial search;
- latest-per-tile selection and per-tile acquisition dates;
- 0.1 m and 2 m asset selection using `gsd`;
- COG media type, EPSG:2056 and checksum metadata;
- download, GDAL inspection and a two-tile 2 m VRT/COG mosaic.
